Requirement on the board: Drive two gauge movements through the driver already on the gauge assembly
Controller resource: 2 timer outputs (step clocks) + 3 GPIO (two direction lines, one reset), via the 74HCT541: 5 lines on PD0 / PD1 / PD4 / PD5 / PD6
Voltage domain: 5V single rail (VDD 4.5-5.5 V); control lines must clear a 3.15 V Vih
Electrical detail: The VID66-08 sits on the gauge assembly, not the main board - confirmed by opening the machine - so a retained board means the driver is INHERITED and the controller drives logic lines rather than motor phases. Step clocks need timer channels - a needle has inertia and an uneven rate reads as stutter. VID6608 datasheet: Vih 3.15 V min and Vil 1.35 V max, both ABSOLUTE across the 4.5-5.5 V supply range rather than scaling with it. The datasheet's own prose says the inputs carry level shifters so the part can run at a higher VDD than the logic driving it - sub-supply drive is intended - but that decouples the threshold from the motor rail without lowering it, and 3.15 V is where the DC table leaves it. So a 3.3 V controller has 150 mV of margin at best, and a common Voh specification of VDD-0.4 V (about 2.9 V) sits BELOW the threshold. Real Voh into the ~10 uA these inputs leak will sit near the rail, but that is typical behaviour and not a guarantee. 3.3 V drive therefore needs level shifting on all five lines, or a part whose own Voh guarantee is checked against 3.15 V, or a bench measurement that turns the typical into an established figure. THE DESIGN USES THE FIRST: all five lines go through a socketed 74HCT541 (DIP-20, on the perfboard, powered from 5V, 100 nF decoupling, 10k pull-ups on /OE1 and /OE2 so the outputs are high-impedance and the needles read zero until firmware enables them) - D19, Chosen. The pin allocation lists the five controller pins (PD0 PD1 PD4 PD5 PD6) as plain GPIO with roles not recorded, which does not provide the timer step clocks stated above (to confirm); its 5V-tolerance analysis was an earlier-controller one flagged RE-CHECK, and the buffer is conservative either way The datasheet also conditions its timing figures on a VSS-to-VDD input swing. Timing: 450 ns min pulse width, 100 ns direction-to-clock setup, 100 ns reset release, rising-edge step of 1/12 degree of SHAFT rotation fixed in silicon, 20 ns glitch filter, and a motor speed ceiling of 7.2 kHz against a 1.1 MHz silicon ceiling - but that 7.2 kHz and the ~280 ohm coil figure are quoted against the VID29 movements the part is sold with, and MOT1/MOT2 have NOT been identified as VID29. RESET is active low and shared across both channels, and the datasheet asks for an external pull-down to hold it low through start-up; no such pull-down is on passive-and-drive-components.csv and the buffer leaves the line high-impedance at boot (to confirm). Needle-referred step and gearing NOT ESTABLISHED - the shaft step is settled at 1/12 degree; what is open is the gearing between shaft and needle. Phase current follows from the VID29 identification above and is bounded meanwhile by the driver's +/-35 mA absolute maximum, though steps-per-sweep is obtainable by counting between the end stops
Suggested placement: Gauge assembly - the driver is already there and stays with it; the perfboard supplies the buffered logic lines only
Serves: MOT1 espresso resistance-to-pour gauge; MOT2 milk temperature gauge

Requirement on the board: Supply every rail the above needs from mains
Controller resource: n/a
Voltage domain: 5V from a Mean Well IRM-10-5; 3V3 from the H743 board's onboard DC-DC
Electrical detail: Mean Well IRM-10-5 (10 W / 2 A, encapsulated, 4.2 kVac isolation, Class II) on a hand-cut single-sided copper-clad carrier, with a recommended T2A slow-blow in the live feed (cold-start inrush 40 A at 230 V) and 47-100 uF low-ESR plus 100 nF across the output (D7, Chosen). It feeds the H743 board's 5V input and all 5V accessories; the 3V3 comes from the board's own DC-DC (3.3-5.5 V in, 1 A max), not an LDO. Typical-based 5V budget ~0.53 A (117 mA H743 + ~39 mA of 3V3 loads + 143 mA relay-module coils, 2 x 71.4 mA for the two valves, not valve solenoid current + ~29 mA SSR drive + ~100 mA indicators + ~75 mA gauge board + ~30 mA buzzer; many items estimated). Worst case with the gauge driver at its datasheet maximum: the VID6608 datasheet gives 76 mA typical and 200 mA maximum at 5-5.5 V, measured against VID29 coil resistances that MOT1/MOT2 have not been identified as carrying, and does not say whether per driver channel or per device, so the old figures doubled both (152 mA typical, 400 mA maximum). Taking the ~75 mA gauge-board term as the typical figure (the BOM mA column carries no gauge row, so that mapping is not recorded there), substituting 200 mA or 400 mA gives about 0.66 A to about 0.86 A, still inside the 2 A rating and up to about 86 % of the 1.0 A derated figure at 70 C. Derating read approximately off the spec sheet: 100% to 50 C, ~75% at 60 C, ~50% at 70 C. The IRM has no earth path, so the entry MOV is required. No 12 V rail appears in the 5V budget or the BOM. The OEM supply is a 9 V 2.5 VA transformer and is nowhere near adequate
